items.rationale: The model keeps nothing between calls; the program keeps the message list and sends it again with each call, including the calendar result.
A new session starts with an empty message list and nothing is saved automatically, so Monday's training is unknown unless the team saved it and loads it back.

items.answer: It keeps the context small and relevant, which costs less per call and avoids burying the answer.
accepted: Because it is cheaper and keeps only relevant text in the context
It saves tokens and window space by loading only what the question needs
Manuals are too long and every token in context is paid for on every call
items.rationale: Everything in the context is billed and takes window space on every call, so bring in only the passages the question needs. Mentioning cost, window space or relevance is enough.
Retrieved chunks are ordinary input; if the search returned the wrong chunk, the model worked from wrong text. The fault is in retrieval, not in forgetting or window size.

items.answer: Short facts such as trained machines with dates or booking preferences, saved to storage and loaded into the system prompt or first message of the next session.
accepted: Trained machines and dates, loaded into the context at the start of the next session
Training status and preferences, read back by the program into the prompt in a new session
items.rationale: Full credit needs two short factual details and the mechanism that the program loads the note into the context. Saying only that the model remembers shows M3.
